correctness.rationale: A commutation class on support S is equivalent to an acyclic orientation of the induced cycle graph C_n[S], since topological orderings of a DAG differ by adjacent swaps of nonedges. Cellular orientation is the increasing vertex-label order, so each group-stabilized cell contributes the sign of its restricted vertex permutation, not just its presence. The augmented cellular Lefschetz formula is valid because the published Boolean complex wedge theorem concentrates reduced homology in top degree n-1 and rank L_n-2. For rotations, periodic vertex supports of length d yield the signed two-state cyclic transfer and forbid the two globally directed full cycles; this produces (-1)^{n+d}(L_d-2), including d=1,2 corrections. Reflected supports fold to paths; inverted edges cannot belong to invariant oriented supports, producing P_{(n-1)/2}, P_{n/2+1}, P_{n/2-2} with the documented signs. Independently enumerated all injective words, commutation classes and oriented simplicial fixed-cell signed traces for all 2n elements for n=3..7; matched exactly, with invariant ranks 0,1,0,2,2. Reviewed source verifier, which extends to n=8, and did not confuse finite checks with universal transfer proof.

value.rationale: Knowing top Betti rank L_n-2 does not identify a group representation; the action on the commutation-class CW cells yields a full uniform character, parity/axis distinctions and exact quotient rational homology. The infinite-family representation and quotient invariants are natural structural data for affine-cycle Boolean complexes and require nontrivial signed transfer arguments, not a bare substitution in the Lucas count.
